judgment_calls: `preChangeSnapshotJson` is defined as an OPAQUE caller-supplied string in this phase (D2.1 is model+repository+migration only, not the live apply-boundary wiring — that is D2.5). The doc comment directs future callers (D2.2/D2.5) toward the existing `buildProfileRevisionFingerprint`-style hash/revision pointer precedent (org_proposal_experiment_service.ts) rather than a raw prior field value, but D2.1 adds no new hashing helper of its own — reusing the established pattern name-checked in the doc comment, not duplicating it, per the ladder ('already in this codebase? reuse it').

Secret redaction is enforced INSIDE the repository (via the existing, already-exported `redactSecrets` from run_outcome_service.ts) rather than trusting every future caller to pre-sanitize — matching the codebase's established defense-in-depth precedent (run_outcome_service.ts redacts its own free-text ledger column the same way). No new redaction implementation was written.

Table has no DB-level state-machine trigger (unlike agent_org_experiment_enrollments / treatment_receipts), matching the simpler `agent_org_proposal_retirements` sidecar precedent — state transitions (guardrail/revert status) are enforced by the repository's `updateStatusAsync`, not a SQL trigger, since D2.1 does not yet define an ordering invariant between guardrailStatus and revertStatus (that lifecycle ordering is D2.2-D2.5's concern) that would need database-level enforcement.

repair-attempt-count capping in `updateStatusAsync` truncates to the FIRST 3 entries of whatever array the caller passes (not the last 3) — the repository takes a full replacement array per call rather than an append primitive, so 'first 3' preserves attempt order; the real D2.3 3-strike loop is expected to stop appending at 3 itself, making this purely a defensive backstop, not the primary gate.

No FK on `profile_id` (matching `agent_org_experiment_treatment_receipts.profile_id`'s existing precedent of no FK there either) — a profile/agent_config row can be deleted independently of its post-apply history without an FK violation; `proposal_id` DOES carry a real FK to `agent_org_proposals(id)` since every PostApplyEvent must reference a real, already-persisted proposal by construction (`createAsync` is only ever called after a real apply).
